races.name: Starman At Tally Ho Stud British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Brokerswood Holiday Park Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Liosa
runners_data.note: Showed ability to win at 6f on good ground (recent win from same conditions) and trainer Zoe Hawkins has a modest 14-day strike rate; sits naturally prominent and a clean early position behind the leader would suit her profile well.

runners_data.name: Secret Oath
runners_data.note: Confirmed sole front-runner in this field — Clive Cox in decent 14-day form (4/28) and Callum Rodriguez takes over; the controlled tempo she will likely set plays to her strengths, though she is noted as racing out of role at this style-fit level, so followers should not over-invest at short odds.

runners_data.name: The Coffee Pod
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse who shows a modest Salisbury/good-ground record (8/15 similar-going runs with no wins); Muir & Grassick yard has a quiet 14-day spell, and from the rear this field's traffic problems make a winning run unlikely.

runners_data.name: The Caribbean
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type who won at 7f on Standard ground but has struggled over 6f on good; Ebrahim Nader takes the ride and the blinkers are a notable headgear flag, though the step back to 6f good-to-firm on turf is not clearly ideal.

runners_data.name: Thunderous Love
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer but the record on good ground (9/6f GOO most recently) and repeated minor placings suggest a horse that finishes without winning; Olivia Tubb's 5lb claim is a modest compensation and the hood headgear change is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Maid In Devon
runners_data.note: Arrives in career-best form having won three of her last four at 6f on good and soft ground — Hector Crouch rides for the in-form Rod Millman yard; her prominent style makes her the ideal tactical tracker in this race shape if she can slot in behind Secret Oath early.

runners_data.name: Lahina Bay
runners_data.note: Won twice at 6f on good ground and is a genuine hold-up finisher by nature, though the crowded closer's camp means she is mapped further forward than she'd choose; Rachel Cook & John Bridger yard quiet in 14 days, and a winning run requires more pace than Secret Oath is likely to generate.

runners_data.name: Red Snapper
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse — placed twice at 6f on good ground — who is pushed into a midfield slot purely by the weight of closers in this field; Charlie Tucker's 7lb claim is appealing but eight days since last run and the redistribution away from his ideal position temper expectations.

runners_data.name: May Encounter
runners_data.note: Consistent finisher in a narrow band (5th, 6th repeatedly on good ground at 6f) who rarely threatens but rarely disgraces; Henry Candy's stable is quiet and the hood headgear is unchanged — a horse that will fill a place frame only if everything goes wrong for others.

runners_data.name: Cici's Secret
runners_data.note: Returns from a 358-day absence with just three career starts all at 6f good ground showing no win or place; Josephine Gordon's experience is a positive but the fitness query after nearly a year off is substantial and the redistribution into midfield compounds the challenge.

races.paceDynamic: Secret Oath is the confirmed lone front-runner in this 6f handicap on good-to-firm ground at Salisbury, and with no genuine rival likely to push forward and challenge for the lead, she can dictate a comfortable, controlled tempo from the front. Maid In Devon and Liosa are the most credible prominent types to track her in second and third, but neither appears likely to apply serious early pressure, meaning the pace is likely to be sustainable rather than searingly fast. The hold-up brigade — Lahina Bay, Red Snapper, May Encounter and Cici's Secret — are all genuine closers by nature but are so numerous they cannot all drop out; several will be forced to race closer than ideal, compromising their chance of a meaningful late challenge. This race shape strongly favours the prominent/tracking profile: with one relaxed pace-setter and a clean run from a handy position, horses able to sit just behind Secret Oath and pick up through the final two furlongs hold the clearest tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Secret Oath Dictates Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Secret Oath is allowed to stride along unchallenged and sets a controlled, even gallop that suits her stamina.
scenarios.body: Secret Oath bowls along in front with Maid In Devon and Liosa tracking in a compact group, and when the closers attempt their challenge in the final furlong the pace has simply not been fast enough early to set up a dramatic late run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Secret Oath's front-running advantage is modest and a horse tracking in second or third is able to quicken past her inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Maid In Devon or Liosa, sitting two lengths off the lead and travelling smoothly, sweeps past the leader approaching the final furlong as Secret Oath slightly ties up; the form of Maid In Devon's recent hat-trick on comparable ground makes her the prime candidate for this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Cuts Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is sharper than expected and a closer can find a clear run to finish with a strong late surge.
scenarios.body: A genuinely redistributed finisher like Lahina Bay — a natural hold-up horse who stays on well in 6f good-ground races — would need a fast-run race and a clean passage to arrive late with purpose; the compressed midfield makes clear runs uncertain.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rank Outsider Causes Upset
scenarios.trigger: If the race is poorly judged tactically and a free-running or lightly raced runner capitalises on a chaotic early phase.
scenarios.body: Cici's Secret returns from 358 days off with an unknown fitness level, while Thunderous Love's headgear change is unproven; if the pace goes awry and the field strings out, an unexpected finisher could emerge from the pack.

watchPoints.text: Maid In Devon's three-timer form at 6f on comparable going makes her the most dangerous rival to Secret Oath if she secures the prominent tracking position without contest.

The sheer volume of hold-up types (Lahina Bay, Red Snapper, May Encounter, Cici's Secret) forced into midfield creates a congested final furlong — watch for traffic problems or interference at a crucial stage.

Secret Oath's STYLE_FIT tag (0.90) means she is racing slightly out of role; if she is outpaced early by a rival pressing forward, the race shape unravels quickly and Maid In Devon becomes the primary beneficiary.

Cici's Secret is 358 days absent — watch how sharply she is supported in the market in the final minutes before the off, as any significant market move would be a meaningful fitness signal from the Charlie Pike yard.

The going report confirms Good To Firm for this 6f contest despite the race card listing Good — in fast conditions Secret Oath's ability to dictate without overextending is the key variable for the dominant scenario.

races.name: Foyles Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Orchard
runners_data.note: Prominent racer trained by Warren Greatrex who brings a course-distance win at Salisbury on good ground and should be ideally positioned tracking Queen's Companion; 26 days off is fine, and good-to-firm is within its comfort zone based on sim-going record of 3/10.

runners_data.name: Double Red
runners_data.note: Henry Candy's five-year-old is naturally a prominent type by style but is genuinely unlikely to secure that position here with Queen's Companion and Orchard already earmarked for the front; recent form reads 5-1844 and its two wins came at this trip, so the distance suits even if the tactical scenario does not.

runners_data.name: Sudbury Hill
runners_data.note: Harry Derham's three-year-old is a confirmed hold-up horse with genuine staying credentials — wins at 17f and 16f on good — but needs the small field to generate enough tempo for a closing run to land; Callum Rodriguez has only one ride for the trainer in the last 14 days and the gelding's last run was a zero in a 12f contest.

runners_data.name: Queen's Companion
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old is the race's lone confirmed pace-setter and carries a STYLE_FIT flag indicating she may be racing outside her most comfortable role; Beckett's trainer strike rate of 12/43 over 14 days is strong, and her most recent win came over today's exact trip on good, making her a credible leader even if she is susceptible to being caught late.

races.paceDynamic: Queen's Companion is the confirmed lone front-runner in this four-runner field and, uncontested, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over Salisbury's 1m2f on good-to-firm ground. Orchard will press from a prominent position just off the leader, while Sudbury Hill — a genuine hold-up operator — will track at the rear with the luxury of watching the pace develop. The field contains more prominent-leaning types than can all occupy that position: Double Red is a natural prominent racer who is likely to find Queen's Companion and Orchard already installed ahead of it, forcing it to race in a less natural role mid-to-rear. With a lone pace-setter controlling a small field on a flat, fast surface, this race shape heavily favours horses who can travel close to the steady early fractions and then unleash a sustained finish — a prominent-to-close profile is the sweet spot, and genuine hold-up horses will need the tempo to lift late enough for them to reel in a well-positioned leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Queen's Companion Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Queen's Companion dictates a measured, uncontested gallop and Orchard cannot sustain a prolonged challenge turning in.
scenarios.body: Queen's Companion leads throughout on good-to-firm at a pace entirely of her own choosing, building a comfort margin that is hard to bridge in only four furlongs of home straight; horses who have tracked close to the leader and can quicken from a handy position are best placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Orchard tracks Queen's Companion efficiently and produces a stronger turn-of-foot in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Orchard, travelling prominently under Mason Paetel, waits for the leader to flatten out and then surges past inside the final furlong on ground that suits its good-to-firm profile; its recent second at this trip on good gives it solid credentials to land this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves honest enough to string out the field and Sudbury Hill's late burst arrives with enough runway.
scenarios.body: Sudbury Hill has an excellent record staying on over longer trips on good ground and, if the front pair set a truly true gallop, Rodriguez can launch a sweeping run from the rear; its trip form (wins at 17f and 16f) suggests stamina is no issue, though the modest field size limits how much tempo is generated.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Disrupted Pace Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Double Red pushes forward early and disrupts Queen's Companion's lead, creating a muddled, uneven gallop.
scenarios.body: Double Red's natural prominent instincts could see it clash for position in the early stages, unsettling the anticipated controlled pace and compressing the field into a bunched finish; in that messy scenario any of the four could be competitive, but Double Red's recent poor form (5-1844) makes it an unreliable beneficiary.

watchPoints.text: Queen's Companion's split-second start is critical — if she is slow away, Orchard could steal the role of leader and Queen's Companion loses her key tactical advantage.

Double Red's natural inclination to race prominently could see it push forward in the first furlong and create unexpected early pressure, disrupting the anticipated controlled pace even in a field of only four.

Sudbury Hill will need Callum Rodriguez to judge the pace precisely from the rear — in a small, slowly-run field a hold-up horse can find itself with too much ground to make up in too short a time on Salisbury's relatively straightforward track.

The going report confirms good-to-firm for this race despite the card listing good — this faster surface marginally favours horses with a prominent style who can dictate their own rhythm rather than closers needing a true end-to-end gallop.

Mason Paetel claims 5lbs on Orchard, giving it an effective weight advantage that could prove significant at the finish if the race develops into a tight duel with the prominently-ridden Queen's Companion.

races.name: Madar Corporation 'Proud To Support Salisbury' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Royal Poetry
runners_data.note: Has won twice over 10-12f on good ground and is the clear pace-controlling force here; the style fit is strong for its role at the front, though having to make all on a flat track over 1m4f against fresher rivals in handicap company is a real test — jockey Seamus Cronin must judge tempo carefully with no rival to push it.

runners_data.name: Virtue Diligence
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse with a placed run on good ground in three starts; the fade-in-finish flag is a meaningful concern at 1m4f when the gallop is likely to be steady, and Hector Crouch will need to find a way to produce it late without being left with too much to do.

runners_data.name: Rossa Raheen
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's three-year-old has placed at 1m2f on good ground and steps up to 1m4f, which the form suggests should suit; a genuine closer by nature whose best chance rests on being close enough through the bend to launch a sustained effort, rather than relying on a sprint finish.

runners_data.name: Traveling Man
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes runner has modest recent form — a third from three runs, all at 1m2f — and is a true hold-up horse by inclination though shown in midfield here because the map is saturated with closers; the step to 1m4f is unexplored and the style fit tag tempers confidence in any scenario requiring it to race prominently.

runners_data.name: Captain Cairney
runners_data.note: Has placed four times from eleven runs and shown genuine consistency at 1m2-1m4f on good and standard ground, making the trip and conditions a positive; wears a p (presumably hood/cheekpieces) and is trained by Muir & Grassick, though like several rivals it is a natural hold-up horse shuffled forward on the map — its actual running will likely come from the rear, and it should be assessed on its closing ability rather than its mapped position.

runners_data.name: Notable Charm
runners_data.note: Marcus Tregoning's charge has the lowest official rating in the field at OR 53 and has yet to win or place in four career starts; a genuine hold-up type in practice though shown in midfield due to redistribution — the trainer's 0-from-3 over 14 days and the horse's uncompetitive recent form make it the most speculative runner in the race, and its best hope is a truly contested finish that it has not yet shown it can exploit.

races.paceDynamic: Royal Poetry is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner 1m4f handicap and will stride to the front unchallenged, setting a sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground at Salisbury. With no genuine rival to press for the lead, Royal Poetry can control tempo entirely on its own terms, conserving energy through the long straight while dictating to the field behind. Virtue Diligence, Rossa Raheen, Traveling Man, Captain Cairney, and Notable Charm are all natural hold-up types, though Traveling Man, Captain Cairney, and Notable Charm have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field cannot accommodate five closers at the rear simultaneously — Royal Poetry is almost certain to secure the rail and dictate alone. This race shape strongly favours the lone front-runner or horses with strong sustained stamina that can track and overhaul a controlled pace, rather than pure late-kickers who depend on a pressured gallop to generate the finish they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Royal Poetry Controls Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Poetry bowls along at a measured tempo with no rival willing to commit to chasing, the race is run to its precise strengths.
scenarios.body: Royal Poetry dictates from the front on good-to-firm ground over a trip it has already won over, denying closers the fast early fractions they need to close.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Overpowers
scenarios.trigger: If a hold-up horse settles just off Royal Poetry's shoulder and uses the controlled pace to produce a sustained run from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: The moderate fractions allow a horse with class and stamina to sit second or third, travel kindly, and simply outstay Royal Poetry in the closing stages without needing a sharp turn of foot.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Poetry sets a stronger-than-expected pace and the field strings out, allowing genuine hold-up horses to pick up the pieces late.
scenarios.body: The increased fractions compromise the front-runner's stamina and open a gap for the best-staying closer to power through, rewarding those who tracked wide and conserved energy deepest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Surprise Develops
scenarios.trigger: If pace collapses entirely and the race becomes a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole, favouring the sharpest accelerator regardless of position.
scenarios.body: A muddling contest with no true pace can neutralise stamina advantages and reward whoever quickens first from a bunched field; however, most runners here lack a sharp turn of foot and the scenario is unlikely to resolve cleanly.

watchPoints.text: Royal Poetry has sole control of tempo — if Seamus Cronin elects to crawl and produce a sprint finish from the front, the entire race shape changes and natural hold-up horses may lack the acceleration to respond.

Captain Cairney and Traveling Man are true hold-up horses mapped to midfield; watch whether either actually secures a forward position at the break or drifts back to their natural ground, as their effective running style will determine which scenario materialises.

Virtue Diligence carries a fade-in-finish flag — if it is held up in a slowly-run race and asked to quicken late, the tendency to weaken in the final furlong could be exposed precisely when it matters most.

The going report consistently reads Good to Firm across all races at Salisbury tonight, which rewards horses with confirmed good-ground form — Royal Poetry (3 wins/places on similar) and Rossa Raheen are best placed on that metric.

Notable Charm and Traveling Man have the lowest combined OR and least experience; if either trades at unusually short odds pre-race, it may signal market intelligence about the headgear or fitness angle that is not fully visible in the form.

races.name: Racing TV Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Lady Of The Isles
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up filly who has been well beaten in recent starts on Good ground, showing sim-going form of zero wins from nine comparable runs; 57 days off the track and a step back in trip from 10f to a mile are both negatives, with hg:hb headgear retained but doing little to arrest the slide.

runners_data.name: Desert Charm
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins on Good ground over this exact mile trip make this the standout form reference in the race; Hector Crouch takes over in the saddle and the horse's sim-going record of three wins from eleven runs understates a very live recent profile — the natural hold-up style means needing something to aim at, which depends on pace being honest.

runners_data.name: It's Life
runners_data.note: Returning after a 295-day absence, this horse has been competing exclusively over extreme distances (13f–18f) in recent starts, making the drop to a flat mile look a significant trip concern; a genuine hold-up type by nature, the crowded rear means it is shown in midfield on the map — racing that far out of both role and distance comfort zone makes its chance fragile.

runners_data.name: Escape Magic
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows's 3-year-old has won two of her last two on Good ground over 7f and steps up to a mile for the first time here; as the race's sole confirmed front-runner, Rodriguez can control the tempo entirely, and the 1/6 trainer T14 strike rate represents a live yard booking — she is racing in the lead role she is built for, making the STYLE_FIT tag largely academic in this specific scenario.

runners_data.name: Outrace
runners_data.note: Six-year-old carrying a headgear flag (hg:p) and returning after 203 days off a deeply uninspiring sequence of zeros, finishing last or near-last in all five recent starts at comparable distances; flagged for fading in the finish, and though pushed to midfield on the map, this horse's true natural position is at the rear where it has been consistently beaten — minimal case for involvement.

runners_data.name: Arvana Belle
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's 3-year-old filly is just 11 days since her last run and holds some sim-going form (1W, 3P from 10 runs on similar ground); a natural hold-up type shown in midfield due to field composition, with headgear (hg:b) in place — the step up from 6-7f trips to a flat mile is an open question but the yard's T14 rate of 8/25 is among the stronger trainer angles in the race.

races.paceDynamic: Escape Magic is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and, with no rival likely to challenge for the lead, Callum Rodriguez can dictate a sustainable, uncontested gallop from the front over Salisbury's flat mile. The going is Good to Firm throughout the card, which will produce a true surface and reward horses travelling comfortably within themselves rather than those grinding from the rear. Desert Charm and Lady Of The Isles are the genuine hold-up types who will need something to aim at in the closing stages, while It's Life, Arvana Belle, and Outrace — all natural hold-up horses — are mapped to midfield purely because the field contains more rear-of-field types than the race shape can accommodate; none of them is a true mid-division racer and their actual chance of influencing proceedings from that position should be discounted accordingly. With a single, uncontested pace-setter likely to control fractions and the closers potentially struggling to get a true strong enough pace to close into, this race shape most favours the horse in front who can regulate the tempo, or a prominent-to-mid tracker who travels fluently and pounces before the hold-up horses can wind up their challenges.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Escape Magic Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Escape Magic jumps cleanly and Rodriguez elects to dictate from the front without pressure, setting a sustainable Good-to-Firm gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Escape Magic, a two-time recent winner over 7f on Good ground, steps up to a mile with no pacemaker to push her and can simply regulate fractions to suit herself, never coming off the bridle until asked.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Catch Moderate Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Escape Magic's uncontested lead produces an even, moderate gallop that leaves genuine hold-up types with enough energy to close through the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Desert Charm, twice a winner over this course and distance on Good ground, is ideally placed to reel in a leader who has not been truly tested; Lady Of The Isles, though out of form, has the profile to hit the line from the rear if pace is genuinely moderate.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistributed Midfielders Interfere
scenarios.trigger: If the congested midfield group — It's Life, Arvana Belle, and Outrace — generate unexpected interference or force an earlier tempo that scrambles the anticipated race shape.
scenarios.body: Racing out of their natural roles, these three horses could unsettle each other or Escape Magic's rhythm, creating a muddled pace scenario where a horse travelling sweetly in second or third, such as Desert Charm, profits from the resulting chaos.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses; Late Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Escape Magic goes too fast early under keenness or the field bunches and the tempo surges, leaving genuine closers with a strongly-run final furlong to target.
scenarios.body: Desert Charm's impressive recent form — back-to-back wins on Good ground over this trip — gives her the strongest late credentials if the race is genuinely run to suit, though this scenario demands a pace pattern that current evidence does not strongly support.

watchPoints.text: Escape Magic's early keenness is the key variable — if Rodriguez cannot settle her cleanly from the gates, she may overcook the pace and hand the race to Desert Charm coming late.
Desert Charm's hold-up style means Hector Crouch must thread through the congested midfield group (It's Life, Arvana Belle, Outrace) in the straight — a troubled passage here would cost her the race.
It's Life returns from 295 days off and drops dramatically in trip from 13-18f to a flat mile; watch for signs of ring-rustiness or early pace panic that could disrupt the field's rhythm.

The Good to Firm surface is consistent across all races on the card — no going deterioration expected, meaning Escape Magic's front-running tactics will be executed on a true, fast surface that rewards her recent winning form.

Outrace (hg:p, 203 days off, finishing last five times consecutively) carries no realistic place claims but monitor for erratic behaviour in the gate or early stages that could interfere with the leaders.
